answers.q1: It replaces the old `return NaN` in `parse` that is reached when the single-value regex has no match/groups. So the compound loop runs only when the input isn't a valid single value; single-unit inputs still use the existing path.
answers.q2: A sticky, case-insensitive regex `part` (flags `/iy`) matching an optionally negative number, optional spaces, and a unit. A lookahead requires the next thing to be another number (`-?\d` or `-?\.\d`) or the end of string.
answers.q3: Each component's matched text is passed recursively to `parse(component[0])` and the results are summed into `total`. The reason: unit conversion stays in the existing single-value code, so the single-unit path is reused as the source of unit conversions.
answers.q4: Each component's sign is taken from whether `component[1]` starts with '-'. If it differs from the sign of earlier parts, the function returns NaN.
answers.q5: It returns `total` only if `count > 1`; otherwise NaN. Spaces between parts are skipped, but if the end is reached and `str` ends with a space, it returns NaN (trailing space is rejected).
answers.q6: `1h -30m`, `-1h 30m`, `1h +30m`, `1h 30`, `1h 30x`, junk, commas, leading or trailing space, and tabs must all be NaN.
answers.q7: Test 3 checks that a 100-character string parses, while a 101-character string and the empty string `''` throw.
answers.q8: The README notes that the `StringValue` type only covers single values, so compound strings are typed only through `parse`. The material doesn't give a specific instruction beyond that, so what users should do is unknown.
answers.q9: The TypeScript type check (`tsc`) could not be run because the TypeScript compiler is not installed.
answers.q10: Order: explore (rg memory file, list files, read sources), edit `src/index.ts`, add `src/compound.test.ts`, edit README, then test (node version, tsc check, git diff --check/stat, `node --test src/compound.test.ts`). Only one test run was needed; it exited 0 and there was no fix phase.
